'''Alaksandar Uładzimieravič Milinkievič''' ({{langx|be|Аляксандар Уладзімеравіч Мілінкевіч}}, {{langx|ru|Александр Владимирович Милинкевич|translit=Aleksandr Vladimirovich Milinkievich}}, 25 July 1947 – 11 August 2026) was a Belarusian politician. He was nominated by the leading [[Belarusian opposition|opposition]] parties in Belarus to run against incumbent [[Alexander Lukashenko]] in the [[2006 Belarusian presidential election|2006 presidential election]].

==Background==
Milinkevič was born in [[Grodno]] on 25 July 1947.{{citation needed|date=August 2026}} After graduating from the [[Yanka Kupala State University of Grodno|University of Grodno]]{{citation needed|date=August 2026}}, he defended his Ph.D. [[Candidate of Sciences|thesis]] at the Institute of Physics of the [[National Academy of Sciences of Belarus]].{{citation needed|date=August 2026}} Between 1980 and 1984 he was in charge of the (then forming) Faculty of [[Physics]] at the [[Setif 1 University|University of Sétif]] in [[Algeria]].{{citation needed|date=August 2026}} He also served as a [[docent]] at the University of Grodno between 1978 and 1980{{citation needed|date=August 2026}}, and then from 1984 on to 1990.{{citation needed|date=August 2026}} At that time he also started to cooperate with local city authorities as chief of one of the committees.{{citation needed|date=August 2026}} Soon he reached the rank of [[deputy mayor]] of the city.{{citation needed|date=August 2026}}

In 2001 he was the chief of staff of [[Siamion Domash]], one of the opposition leaders running for president in the [[2001 Belarusian presidential election|2001 presidential elections of Belarus]].{{citation needed|date=August 2026}} In October 2005 he was chosen by the [[United Democratic Forces of Belarus]] as the joint candidate of the [[Opposition (politics)|opposition]] in the [[2006 Belarusian presidential election|presidential elections of 2006]].{{citation needed|date=August 2026}}

[[File:Alaksandar Milinkievic.jpg|upright|thumb|Alaksandr Milinkievič in [[Poland]], 30 March 2006]]
On 12 December 2006 he was awarded the [[Sakharov Prize]] by the [[European Parliament]].

He was the recipient of the seventh [[Hanno R. Ellenbogen Citizenship Award]], awarded annually by [[Prague Society for International Cooperation]] and the {{ill|Global Panel Foundation|de}}<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://praguesociety.org/content/hre-awards-history-winners-origin |title=The Prague Society &#124; Promoting a global approach to business, politics and academia in Central Europe through transparent networking and off the record dialogue |access-date=2015-08-12 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140903124001/http://praguesociety.org/content/hre-awards-history-winners-origin |archive-date=2014-09-03 |url-status=dead }}</ref>, as well as the recipient of the [[Decoration of Honor Meritorious for Polish Culture]].<ref>{{cite web |url = http://who.bdg.by/obj.php?&kod=498 |title = МИЛИНКЕВИЧ Александр Владимирович |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150406053514/http://who.bdg.by/obj.php?&kod=498 |archive-date = 2015-04-06 |work = Кто есть кто в Республике Беларусь |language = ru |access-date = 2011-09-15}}</ref>

Milinkievič died from complications of surgery on 11 August 2026, at the age of 79.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Тихановская о смерти Милинкевича: «Это огромная и горькая потеря для всех нас» |url=https://ru.belsat.eu/94799493/tihanovskaya-o-smerti-milinkevicha |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260812170808/https://ru.belsat.eu/94799493/tihanovskaya-o-smerti-milinkevicha |archive-date=2026-08-12 |website=ru.belsat.eu}}</ref> He was buried at [[Powązki Military Cemetery]] in [[Warsaw]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://nashaniva.com/402880|title=Удава Мілінкевіча: «Аляксандр абавязкова вернецца на радзіму, дадому. Надыдзе час»|website=[[Nasha Niva]]|language=be}}</ref>

==Campaign for presidency==
In October 2005, at a Congress of Democratic Forces, roughly 900 delegates from various political and civil society groups met in the capital [[Minsk]] to pick a single opposition candidate for the 2006 Presidential election.{{citation needed|date=August 2026}} Milinkievič won over three other political leaders at the meeting (including [[Stanislav Shushkevich]] and [[Anatoly Lebedko]]).{{citation needed|date=August 2026}} The unification process has the aim of selecting a single opposition figure who would run against President Lukashenko, who has run Belarus for over a decade. Belarus' opposition forces had previously tried to field a single candidate in the [[2001 Belarusian presidential election|2001 presidential elections]].

Milinkievič compared his campaign to that of another pro-Western opposition candidate in neighboring [[Ukraine]], [[Viktor Yushchenko]], whose victory in late 2004 was dubbed the "[[Orange Revolution]]". Although disappointment in Yushchenko's government culminated in a political crisis in September 2005 amid renewed allegations of mass graft coupled with a worsening economic situation, Milinkievič called that year's events in Ukraine an inspiration for his supporters.<ref>[http://today.reuters.co.uk/news/newsArticle.aspx?type=worldNews&storyID=2005-09-28T163259Z_01_HO859543_RTRUKOC_0_UK-UKRAINE.xml&archived=False Reuters]{{dead link|date=July 2021|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> "We believe that Belarus will be next after… Ukraine," he told [[Associated Press]].<ref>Tom Hundley [https://www.chicagotribune.com/2005/10/04/bold-moves-in-belarus/ Bold moves in Belarus] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241222191521/https://www.chicagotribune.com/2005/10/04/bold-moves-in-belarus/ |date=2024-12-22 }} October 04, 2005</ref>

However, opposition leaders realized that an uphill struggle lay ahead, despite their support from U.S.-funded [[Non-governmental organization|NGOs]].{{citation needed|date=August 2026}} Lukashenko's [[market socialism]] economy has significant support in rural areas of the country. Belarus is one of the few areas of the former [[Soviet Union]] where the country's social welfare network remains virtually unchanged since the Soviet era.<ref>{{cite news|title=Opposition in Belarus Unites to Select Candidate for President |url=http://www.voanews.com/english/2005-10-02-voa33.cfm |work=[[Voice of America]] |date=2005-10-02 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20051003092328/http://voanews.com/english/2005-10-02-voa33.cfm |archive-date=2005-10-03 }}</ref>

In the [[2006 Belarusian presidential election|2006 presidential election]] official results gave Milinkievič 6% of the vote against 83% for the incumbent Lukashenko. Confiscation of his leaflets during the campaign was found by the [[UN Human Rights Committee]] to violate his rights.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.bayefsky.com/pdf/belarus_t5_iccpr_1553_2007.pdf|title=HRC views CCPR/C/95/D/1553/2007|access-date=2012-01-03|archive-date=2012-03-03|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120303065856/http://www.bayefsky.com/pdf/belarus_t5_iccpr_1553_2007.pdf|url-status=live}}</ref>

In January 2006 Milinkievič was invited to [[Paris]] by the French government.{{citation needed|date=August 2026}}He met with the [[French Minister of Foreign Affairs]],{{citation needed|date=August 2026}} and gave numerous interviews{{vague|date=August 2026}} to Western media,{{citation needed|date=August 2026}} including a TV interview to [[Euronews]].{{citation needed|date=August 2026}} Milinkievič, just like any other opposition activist, had absolutely no TV access inside Belarus, as the media in Belarus is state-controlled. The only exception when he was allowed to appear on Belarusian television was his pre-election speech in 2006.{{citation needed|date=August 2026}} Earlier, he had already met the new [[Poland|Polish]] prime minister [[Kazimierz Marcinkiewicz]]{{citation needed|date=August 2026}}, and the president of [[Lithuania]] [[Valdas Adamkus]].{{citation needed|date=August 2026}} In February 2006 he also met the President of the [[European Commission]], [[José Manuel Barroso]],{{citation needed|date=August 2026}} [[German Chancellor]] [[Angela Merkel]],{{citation needed|date=August 2026}} [[Javier Solana]]{{citation needed|date=August 2026}}, and several other top European politicians.{{specify|date=August 2026}}{{citation needed|date=August 2026}} His campaign received the backing first of the Polish government and later that of prominent [[EU]] officials.{{citation needed|date=January 2012}}

==Personal life==
Married to Inna Kuley,{{When|date=July 2025}} he had two sons from a previous marriage.{{citation needed|date=August 2026}} Aside from his native [[Belarusian language|Belarusian]] Milinkievič also spoke [[Polish language|Polish]], [[French language|French]], and [[Russian language|Russian]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Біяграфія Аляксандр Мілінкевіч беларускі палітык і навукоўца. |url=http://by.milinkevich.org/about/biography/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060404060908/http://by.milinkevich.org/about/biography/ |archive-date=4 April 2006 |language=be |trans-title=Biography Alaksandar Milinkievičh Belarusian politician and scientist}}</ref>

==Persecution==
In April 2006, Milinkievič was jailed by the government for 15 days for taking part in an unsanctioned rally.<ref>{{cite web |title=Court imprisons Belarus opposition leader |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2006/04/27/world/europe/court-imprisons-belarus-opposition-leader.html |work=[[New York Times]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221201144543/https://www.nytimes.com/2006/04/27/world/europe/court-imprisons-belarus-opposition-leader.html |archive-date=1 December 2022 |date=27 April 2006}}</ref>

On 23 November 2006 government police detained Milinkievič three times as he traveled around [[Vitebsk Region]] with a local opposition activist who was accused of causing a fatal [[Hit and run (vehicular)|hit-and-run]] accident in the past.<ref>{{cite news|title=Belarus opposition leader Milinkevich detained, spokesman says |url=http://www.iht.com/articles/ap/2006/11/23/europe/EU_GEN_Belarus_Opposition.php |work=[[International Herald Tribune]] |date=2006-11-23 |access-date=2009-05-13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061124002206/http://www.iht.com/articles/ap/2006/11/23/europe/EU_GEN_Belarus_Opposition.php |archive-date=2006-11-24 |url-status=live }}</ref>  On 29 November 2006 police detained Milinkievič at a Minsk airport after he returned from a [[NATO]] summit in [[Riga]]. He was accused of having a forged  passport.<ref>{{cite news|title=Belarus' main opposition leader detained by authorities |url=http://www.iht.com/articles/ap/2006/11/29/europe/EU_GEN_Belarus_Opposition.php |work=International Herald Tribune |date=2006-11-29 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080514035735/http://www.iht.com/articles/ap/2006/11/29/europe/EU_GEN_Belarus_Opposition.php |archive-date=2008-05-14 }}</ref>

On 4 December 2006 Milinkievič was detained in [[Beloozyorsk]] on suspicion of [[illegal drug trade]] activity.<ref>{{cite news|title=Police briefly detain Belarusian opposition leader for 3rd time in 2 weeks: spokesman |url=http://www.iht.com/articles/ap/2006/12/04/europe/EU_GEN_Belarus_Opposition.php |work=International Herald Tribune |date=2006-12-04 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080514035736/http://www.iht.com/articles/ap/2006/12/04/europe/EU_GEN_Belarus_Opposition.php |archive-date=2008-05-14 }}</ref>

On 6 January 2007 Milinkevich was arrested twice: first on the suspicion of drunk driving (he was found to be sober) and then on the suspicion of being involved in a traffic accident.<ref>{{cite news|title=Police detain Belarusian opposition leader twice in one day, spokesman says |url=http://www.iht.com/articles/ap/2007/01/06/europe/EU-GEN-Belarus-Opposition.php |work=International Herald Tribune |date=2007-01-06 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080514035744/http://www.iht.com/articles/ap/2007/01/06/europe/EU-GEN-Belarus-Opposition.php |archive-date=2008-05-14 }}</ref> On 29 January 2007 Milinkevich said he was fined $2,200 after being tried in absentia for leaving Belarus illegally. He called it "revenge by Lukashenko".<ref>{{cite news|title=Belarusian opposition leader fined over alleged border infraction |url=http://www.iht.com/articles/ap/2007/01/29/europe/EU-GEN-Belarus.php |work=International Herald Tribune |date=2007-01-29 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080514035750/http://www.iht.com/articles/ap/2007/01/29/europe/EU-GEN-Belarus.php |archive-date=2008-05-14 }}</ref>
